A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same algebraic graph-cover framework and Sieve Neural Networks. The complete text, equations, figures, tables, v1 proof section, and v2 Appendices A–F support comparison despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: Section VI reports original SNN results on SRG, CSL, BREC, and six TUD graph-classification datasets.

after.justification: Section 6 retains original isomorphism and classification results and adds label-propagation experiments on six node datasets. Table 4 also reports preprocessing runtimes.

M1.justification: The original cover-to-matrix pipeline and SNN alpha/beta constructions remain. However, Sections 5.3–5.4 add sieve-adapted WL initialization and distinct random-walk and partition-flow operator constructions, substantially expanding the procedural scope beyond v1's sieve and k-hop constructions.

E1.justification: v2 adds node-label propagation on Cora, CiteSeer, PubMed, ogbn-arxiv, AmazonPhoto, and Actor, extending coverage to larger graphs and an explicitly heterophilic setting. MUTAG and PTC classification are removed; SRG, CSL, BREC, NCI1, IMDB-B, IMDB-M, and PROTEINS remain.

E2.justification: The new topology probe evaluates adjacency-polynomial comparison operators Ad, Ad², Ad+Ad², and Ad+Ad²+Ad³ against SNN operators in Table 2. This adds a substantial controlled comparison family. Comparator membership in the retained SRG, BREC, and TUD comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 introduces one-step, parameter-free label propagation with alpha=1, training-label initialization, and three operator normalizations. SRG embeddings change from four summaries to six, and BREC embeddings from determinant/variance to the same six summaries. These are reported protocol revisions despite unchanged perfect discrimination outcomes. Shared TUD sieve depths, gamma=0.5, and tenfold cross-validation remain.

E4.justification: Table 2 adds controlled analyses of operator structure, propagation depth, and normalization, testing whether longer polynomial walks explain sieve performance. Table 4 adds measured construction-cost analysis. v1 lacks these empirical analyses; its illustrative MPNN counterexample survives in Appendix D.2.

E5.justification: v2 explicitly identifies the classification uncertainty quantities as standard deviations and explains the lack of fold-level evidence for significance testing. The retained numerical uncertainties and tenfold cross-validation are unchanged; no additional runs, seeds, confidence intervals, or completed significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: v2 adds all Table 2 propagation accuracies and Table 4 runtimes; for example, Actor reaches 0.254 versus 0.196 for the best classical operator. It removes MUTAG and PTC results, including SNN's 96.11±3.3 and 77.3±4.1. Shared TUD scores and perfect isomorphism outcomes remain numerically unchanged, although SRG/BREC embeddings differ.

T1.justification: Most foundational theorems and proofs are retained or relocated. v2 adds the formal sieve-adapted WL definition and associated monotonicity reasoning, and Appendix D.3 introduces an O(|E||V|) bound for depth-one beta configurations instead of v1's general sparse O(|E||V|²) account. The short proof of v1 Theorem V.3 is omitted although its statement remains as E.2.2.

C1.justification: The central contributions—algebraic covers, their matrix interpretation, and SNN—remain. v2 adds the controlled topology probe as an explicit contribution and headline empirical claim, while emphasizing SNN as a fixed, non-learned exemplar of the broader framework.

C2.justification: Beyond v1's brief overfitting caution, v2 discusses saturation disrupting within-class similarity, dense-operator memory and computation costs, and possible sparsification. It adds interpretations of propagation depth and heterophily, distinguishes framework expressivity from bounded WL refinement, and cautions that overlapping classification uncertainties do not establish statistical superiority.

D1.justification: v2 adds Algorithms 1–4, dataset statistics, preprocessing timings, and Table 5's learning rates, batch sizes, layer counts, dropout, hidden widths, and Colab CPU environment. These newly document implementation rather than establish changes to retained training settings. Conversely, v1's explicit repository link and vector-valued edge-feature implementation guidance are omitted.

R1.justification: The main related-work families and comparison with higher-order GNNs remain. v2 adds focused references on label propagation, heterophily, newer topological frameworks, and graph reduction/sparsification, while removing references associated with oversmoothing, category-theory background, and edge-feature pretraining. Publication updates to retained works do not constitute new citations.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and substantial methodological prose are rewritten with clearer thematic headings and staged explanations. Construction details, examples, submonoid results, and proofs are reorganized into Appendices A–F. The framework acronym changes from GGNN to GkGNN.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column presentation. v1 Figures 3–4 are combined into v2 Figure 2, other illustrations move to appendices, and a new random-walk diagram appears. SRG/BREC tables are merged, the classification table loses two columns and changes highlighting, and new propagation, runtime, and hyperparameter tables are added.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the framework easier to understand and assess through clearer exposition, controlled operator comparisons, explicit training details, and substantive limitations and statistical cautions. These provide a supported quality gain. The gain is tempered by removing two classification datasets and the code-access pointer, while leaving the new propagation experiment's data splits unspecified; reproducibility and evidential completeness therefore remain limited.
